Force Traveller EV Launch In Q1 2027 - Rs 3,000 Cr Investment

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • It was in 2020 when Force Motors showcased their T1N monocoque electric platform and promised electric Traveller vans.
  • The company has been testing these next generation Traveller EV and a launch is expected to happen in Q1 of 2027 between January 2027 and March 2027, as confirmed by Managing Director Prasan Firodia.
  • Official reporting verified via Rushlane.com news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

It was in 2020 when Force Motors showcased their T1N monocoque electric platform and promised electric Traveller vans. The company has been testing these next generation Traveller EV and a launch is expected to happen in Q1 of 2027 between January 2027 and March 2027, as confirmed by Managing Director Prasan Firodia.

📌 The Core Development

It has to be noted that Force Motors has revealed the e-Traveller Smart Citibus EV powered by a 70 kWh battery pack with 18% gradability, 14+D seating config, 3,350 mm long wheelbase and 5,415 mm length. It will have electrically operated jack-knife door, AC, 1.8m standing height, spacious interiors, external and internal cameras, GPS and more amenities.

As confirmed by Force Motors Managing Director Prasan Firodia, the company has developed the electric Traveller platform on which multiple Force electric vans will be launched. This electric van platform will also spawn special application vehicles like electric ambulances for intracity operations.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

The development process of Traveller EV platform is complete and are currently undergoing final testing and homologation process with ARAI. While finer details about the Force Traveller EVs and the launch were not revealed, they are set to make a grand debut in Q1 of 2027, between January 2027 and March 2027.

An electric version of the more premium Urbania is also under development and it will launch within a few months of the launch of Traveller EV. Adaption of electric mobility in larger commercial vehicles over Diesel fuel will be gradual over the years, when compared to smaller cars and SUVs.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

However, there are a few applications like school buses, employee transportation and intracity ambulances where electric mobility plays a viable role. Tourism and small inter-city applications are probable applications for electric powertrains right now. Other than the e-Traveller Smart Citibus EV, more variants are likely to launch.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Force Motors has pledged an investment of Rs 3,000 Crores across engineering, electrification, hybrid driveline technology and digitisation. Also, the company has committed to manufacturing capacity expansion that will accommodate increased demand in the future with Traveller EV and Urbania EV.
